knowledge:
- key_parameters: K=The number of cell clusters to estimate ;; L=The number of feature modules to estimate ;; x=A SingleCellExperiment object or sparse count matrix containing filtered cells ;; background=A SingleCellExperiment object or sparse count matrix containing raw/droplet counts (including empty droplets) used to estimate ambient RNA ;; delta=A numeric vector of length two representing the Dirichlet priors for native and contamination proportions in decontX ;; estimateDelta=Logical indicating whether to update delta during decontX iterations ;; bestOnly=Logical indicating whether to return only the chain with the best log likelihood in celdaGridSearch
- alternatives: singleCellTK is recommended for importing raw/filtered matrices from CellRanger, STARsolo, BUStools, etc. ;; Seurat is mentioned for downstream analysis, and the documentation provides instructions for converting data between Seurat and SingleCellExperiment objects.
- when_to_use: Use celda when you want to perform simultaneous co-clustering of cells and genes (modules) on sparse scRNA-seq count data. Use DecontX when droplet-based scRNA-seq data suffers from ambient RNA contamination from the cell suspension.
- pitfalls: DecontX contamination estimation depends heavily on cell cluster labels; inappropriate clustering (e.g., too many or too few clusters) can affect accuracy. ;; If cell IDs in the background matrix match those in the filtered matrix, decontX removes them, but if no cell IDs are available, it treats the entire background as empty droplets. ;; Decontaminated counts from DecontX are floating-point numbers and must be rounded to integers before being added to a Seurat object.

workflows.name: celda_bi_clustering
workflows.intent: Perform simultaneous bi-clustering of cells and genes into modules, optimize the number of clusters (K) and modules (L), and visualize the co-expression patterns.
input: simsce (SingleCellExperiment object containing a raw count assay)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter features using selectFeatures ;; 2. Optimize the number of modules (L) using recursiveSplitModule and plot perplexity/RPC ;; 3. Optimize the number of cell clusters (K) using recursiveSplitCell and plot perplexity/RPC ;; 4. Alternatively, perform a parameter grid search using celdaGridSearch ;; 5. Subset the best model using subsetCeldaList ;; 6. Generate 2D embeddings using celdaUmap or celdaTsne ;; 7. Visualize clusters, modules, and features using plotDimReduceCluster, plotDimReduceModule, plotDimReduceFeature, celdaHeatmap, celdaProbabilityMap, and moduleHeatmap ;; 8. Retrieve feature-to-module assignments using featureModuleLookup and recode cluster labels using recodeClusterZ.
workflows.code:
simsce <- selectFeatures(simsce)
sce <- celda_CG(x = simsce, K = 5, L = 10, verbose = FALSE, nchains = 1)
sce <- celdaUmap(sce)
plotDimReduceCluster(x = sce, reducedDimName = "celda_UMAP")
plotDimReduceModule(x = sce, reducedDimName = "celda_UMAP", rescale = TRUE)
plotDimReduceFeature(x = sce, reducedDimName = "celda_UMAP", normalize = TRUE, features = "Gene_1")
plot(celdaHeatmap(sce = sce, nfeatures = 10))
celdaProbabilityMap(sce)
moduleHeatmap(sce, featureModule = c(1,2), topCells = 100)
moduleSplit <- recursiveSplitModule(simsce, initialL = 2, maxL = 15)
plotGridSearchPerplexity(moduleSplit)
plotRPC(moduleSplit)
moduleSplitSelect <- subsetCeldaList(moduleSplit, params = list(L = 10))
cellSplit <- recursiveSplitCell(moduleSplitSelect, initialK = 3, maxK = 12, yInit = celdaModules(moduleSplitSelect))
plotGridSearchPerplexity(cellSplit)
plotRPC(cellSplit)
sce <- subsetCeldaList(cellSplit, params = list(K = 5, L = 10))
cgs <- celdaGridSearch(simsce, paramsTest = list(K = seq(4, 6), L = seq(9, 11)), cores = 1, model = "celda_CG", nchains = 2, maxIter = 100, verbose = FALSE, bestOnly = TRUE)
plotGridSearchPerplexity(cgs)
sce <- subsetCeldaList(cgs, params = list(K = 5, L = 10))
featureModuleLookup(sce, feature = c("Gene_99"))
sceZRecoded <- recodeClusterZ(sce, from = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5), to = c(2, 1, 3, 4, 5))

workflows.name: decontx_decontamination
workflows.intent: Estimate and remove ambient RNA contamination from single-cell RNA-seq data and visualize the decontamination results.
input: sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing a raw count assay)
sce.raw (Optional SingleCellExperiment object containing raw/droplet background counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Run decontX with or without background counts ;; 2. Retrieve decontaminated counts using decontXcounts ;; 3. Visualize cell clusters and contamination levels on UMAP using plotDimReduceCluster and plotDecontXContamination ;; 4. Compare marker gene expression before and after decontamination using plotDecontXMarkerPercentage and plotDecontXMarkerExpression ;; 5. (Optional) Adjust priors using the delta parameter to force more aggressive decontamination.
workflows.code:
sce <- decontX(sce)
sce <- decontX(sce, background = sce.raw)
umap <- reducedDim(sce, "decontX_UMAP")
plotDimReduceCluster(x = sce$decontX_clusters, dim1 = umap[, 1], dim2 = umap[, 2])
plotDecontXContamination(sce)
plotDecontXMarkerPercentage(sce, markers = markers, groupClusters = cellTypeMappings, assayName = "counts")
plotDecontXMarkerPercentage(sce, markers = markers, groupClusters = cellTypeMappings, assayName = "decontXcounts")
plotDecontXMarkerPercentage(sce, markers = markers, groupClusters = cellTypeMappings, assayName = c("counts", "decontXcounts"))
plotDecontXMarkerExpression(sce, markers = markers[["Monocyte_Markers"]], groupClusters = cellTypeMappings, ncol = 3)
sce.delta <- decontX(sce, delta = c(9, 20), estimateDelta = FALSE)
